title: Foundation: skeleton, store, HTTP seam, response classification, network guard
test_command: npm ci && npm run lint && npm run test:foundation
body:
## What to build

The floor the other four cards stand on: the project skeleton, the SQLite store, the single module in the repository allowed to open a socket, response classification, and the harness that makes *"this suite never reaches OzBargain"* a mechanised fact rather than a promise.

Specification: `design.md` 2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 4, 9. Fixtures: all of `fixtures/README.md`.

### 1. Skeleton

- `package.json` - module type, engines `>=24`, the scripts below.
- Dependencies pinned once, here, for the whole project so later cards do not each pick their own: `next`, `react`, `react-dom`, `jose`, `cheerio`, `fast-xml-parser`, `nodemailer`. Dev: `eslint`, `eslint-config-next`.
- `next.config.mjs` with a standalone output target - card 5's image depends on it. ESLint flat config in `eslint.config.mjs`; `next lint` is not used.
- Scripts: `lint` runs `eslint .`; `test:foundation` runs `node --test --import ./test/support/no-network.js test/unit/foundation test/guards`.
- Commit `package-lock.json`.

### 2. `lib/config.js`

Reads 9.1's values from the environment, validates them, and returns a frozen object. **These key names are contractual - later cards import them:**

`OZB_DEALS_FEED_URL` (default `https://www.ozbargain.com.au/deals/feed`), `OZB_FRONT_FEED_URL` (default `https://www.ozbargain.com.au/feed`), `OZB_CLASSIFIEDS_URL` (default `https://www.ozbargain.com.au/classified`), `OZB_USER_AGENT`, `OZB_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (default 300), `OZB_CLASSIFIEDS_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (default 3600), `OZB_DB_PATH` (default `/data/ozbargain.db`), `OZB_SNAPSHOT_PATH` (default `/data/ozbargain-snapshot.db`), `OZB_HEALTHCHECK_SECRET`, `CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN`, `CF_ACCESS_AUD`, `OZB_ICON_ROUTE_PUBLIC` (default false), and the provider credentials listed in 9.1.

The default User-Agent names the application, its version and a contact URL, per 3.8 - for example `OzBargainHunter/<version> (+https://ozb.gallagherhome.au)`. **No browser impersonation, ever** (D14).

`OZB_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS` below 300 is a **startup error**, not a silent clamp. 3.2 says never less than five minutes.

### 3. `lib/clock.js` and `lib/random.js`

Two seams, both injected everywhere:

- `systemClock()` and `fixedClock(isoString)`, each exposing `now()` returning a `Date`.
- `systemRandom()` and `seededRandom(seed)`, each exposing `next()` in the half-open unit interval, so backoff jitter is deterministic under test.

**No module in this repository calls `Date.now()`, `new Date()` or `Math.random()` for behaviour.** Cards 2, 3 and 5 all depend on being able to freeze time.

### 4. `lib/store/`

`openStore(options)` takes a path and a clock, applies migrations, and returns the data-access object.

- **WAL mode** (4.3) and `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000` on every connection. Two processes write to this file (2.2); the busy timeout is what stops the loser throwing.
- **Migrations from version 1** (4.3), tracked in a `schema_version` table, idempotent and forward-only.
- Tables: `deals`, `observations`, `rules`, `ledger`, `feed_state`, `poll_state`, `failures`, `pending_alerts` - the eight entities of 4.1, with the fields listed there, including a nullable `front_page_first_seen` on `deals`. Plus three tables 4.1 does not enumerate but 6.7, 7.1 screen 6 and 9.2 require: `providers` (kind, config, selected, enabled, consecutive_failures, disabled_at, last_error), `settings` (key and value, holding 9.2's UI-editable configuration including the freebie checkbox), and `suppressions` (poll_at, node_id, rule_id, kind, detail - where kind is one of repost, expired, cooldown, muted, near_miss).
- **Every timestamp column stores UTC** as an ISO-8601 Z string (4.3). Melbourne is a display concern only.
- `pruneObservations(now)` deletes counter observations older than 7 days (4.2). Deals and ledger rows are never pruned.
- `writeSnapshot(path)` writes a consistent single-file snapshot with `VACUUM INTO`, per 4.3. That snapshot is what an external backup is expected to capture.

### 5. `lib/http/transport.js` - the seam

**This is the only module in the repository permitted to perform network I/O.** Everything else receives a transport.

`createHttpTransport(options)` takes a user agent and returns an object with one method, `fetch(url, options)`, resolving to a response carrying `status`, lower-cased `headers`, a `body` string and a `bytes` count. Implement it on Node's built-in `fetch` - and see the note under D14 in `decisions.md`; the old `curl_cffi` / `tls-client` question does not survive the stack change, because D14 already forbids what those tools are for.

`test/support/fixtureTransport.js` provides `createFixtureTransport(routes)`, the substitute every test uses. `routes` maps an exact URL string to a response descriptor: a status, headers, and either a body string or a path under `fixtures/`. **A request for a URL the map does not contain throws.** That is deliberate - it is how later cards prove the poller never asks for page 2.

### 6. `lib/http/client.js`

`createOzbClient(deps)` takes a transport, a store, a clock, a random and config, and implements 3.3 and 3.4:

- **Deny list, hard-coded**: `/api/`, `/ozbapi/`, `/search/`, `/comment/`, `/goto/`, `/privatemsg/`, `/user/login`. Any of them throws `DeniedPathError` **before the transport is consulted**.
- **Conditional requests are mandatory.** Every request carries `If-None-Match` and `If-Modified-Since` from `feed_state` for that URL; a 200 updates them.
- One request in flight at a time, with a pause between requests, default 3 seconds, taken from the clock rather than by sleeping in tests.
- `Retry-After` honoured on 429 and 503; everything else backs off exponentially with jitter drawn from the injected random.
- **A Cloudflare block latches the client off.** After one, every subsequent call throws `BlockedError` without touching the transport, until explicitly cleared. 3.5: never treated as transient.
- Every request's URL, response class and timestamp is logged.

### 7. `lib/http/classify.js`

Pure. `classifyResponse(response)` returns exactly one of `ok`, `not_modified`, `cloudflare_block`, `permission_denied`, `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `transient`. 3.5 is the specification. The distinction that matters most is between the two kinds of 403: they differ by two orders of magnitude in body size and share no markup - see `fixtures/README.md` section 3.

Parse failure is *not* classified here. A body that will not parse is still an `ok` response at the HTTP layer; card 2 marks it unparseable after parsing.

### 8. The network guard - `test/support/no-network.js`

Loaded through `node --test --import ./test/support/no-network.js`. It replaces `globalThis.fetch`, `http.request`, `https.request`, `net.Socket.prototype.connect` and `dns.lookup` with wrappers that throw `NetworkBlockedError` for any host other than `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `::1`, and it sets a sentinel on `globalThis`. Loopback stays open because card 5's integration tests run a real server there.

## Acceptance criteria

- `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run test:foundation` passes on Node 24. A test asserts the Node major version is at least 24 and fails with a message naming the requirement.
- A fresh database is created at schema version 1 with all eleven tables; running migrations again changes nothing; `PRAGMA journal_mode` returns `wal` and `PRAGMA busy_timeout` returns at least 5000.
- `pruneObservations` deletes an observation stamped 8 days before the frozen now, and leaves one stamped 6 days before it.
- `writeSnapshot` produces a file that opens as a valid database with identical row counts, and the source database is still in WAL mode afterwards.
- Each of the seven denied paths throws `DeniedPathError` with the fixture transport's call count still at zero.
- After a 200 carrying an `ETag` and a `Last-Modified`, the next request for that URL carries `If-None-Match` and `If-Modified-Since` with those exact values. A 304 returns `not_modified`, a zero-length body, and leaves `feed_state` untouched.
- Classification, asserted against real bodies:
  - `fixtures/http/r0.xml` at 200 gives `ok`
  - an empty body at 304 gives `not_modified`
  - `fixtures/http/derived/cloudflare-1010.txt` at 403 with a `server: cloudflare` header gives `cloudflare_block`, **and not** `permission_denied`
  - `fixtures/http/cls403.html` at 403 gives `permission_denied`, **and not** `cloudflare_block`
  - `fixtures/http/feed_classifieds_feed.xml` at 404 gives `not_found`
  - `fixtures/http/pg11.xml` at 500 gives `transient`
  - a 429 carrying `Retry-After: 120` gives `rate_limited` with the 120 surfaced to the caller
- After a `cloudflare_block`, the next two client calls throw `BlockedError` and the transport call count does not increase.
- Backoff with `seededRandom(1)` produces the same delay sequence on two runs, and the sequence is strictly increasing before jitter is applied.

## Tests this card must include

Under `test/unit/foundation/`: config validation, store schema and migrations, retention, snapshot, the deny list, conditional requests, classification with one case per class against the real fixture, backoff determinism, and the Cloudflare latch.

Under `test/guards/` - these run with **every** card's test command, from here on:

1. `no-network.test.js` - asserts the sentinel is set, so deleting the `--import` flag fails the suite rather than silently disarming it; asserts a fetch of `https://www.ozbargain.com.au/deals/feed` rejects with `NetworkBlockedError`; asserts a `127.0.0.1` request is permitted.
2. `test-scripts.test.js` - reads `package.json` and asserts **every** script whose name starts with `test` contains `--import ./test/support/no-network.js`.
3. `node-version.test.js` - the engines floor.
notes:
Read `design.md` and `fixtures/README.md` before writing any code. `design.md` is normative: where it and this card disagree, `design.md` wins - say so in the PR instead of quietly choosing.

Project-wide rules, identical on every card:
- **Node.js 24 LTS. ESM JavaScript, no TypeScript.** `package.json` declares a module type and an engines floor of `>=24`.
- **SQLite is `node:sqlite`**, built into Node 24. No `better-sqlite3`, no ORM. An ExperimentalWarning on import is expected; do not change drivers because of it.
- **Tests run on `node --test`.** No Jest, Vitest, Mocha, Chai or Sinon. Node's `assert/strict` and the `node:test` mock and timer facilities are enough.
- **The test suite never reaches `ozbargain.com.au`.** Every `test:*` script must carry `--import ./test/support/no-network.js`, and a guard test asserts it does.
- **Two processes, one container** (design 2.2, D61). The Next.js server serves the UI; a separate worker owns the poll loop. **Polling from a route handler, middleware, instrumentation hook or revalidation is a build error**, not a style choice.
- Add a dependency, update `package-lock.json` in the same commit.

**This card fixes names the other four import**: the `lib/config.js` keys, `createHttpTransport`, `createFixtureTransport`, `createOzbClient`, `openStore`, `systemClock` and `fixedClock`. Renaming any of them later means editing four cards' worth of code, so get them right here.

`fixtures/` is already populated and is not yours to regenerate - the scripts in `fixtures/tools/` exist to document provenance. Do not modify anything under `fixtures/http/` except by adding to `fixtures/http/derived/` through the existing script.

title: Acquisition: feed and classifieds parsers, session handling, the poll cycle
test_command: npm ci && npm run lint && npm run test:acquisition
body:
## What to build

Everything that turns a captured HTTP response into rows in the database. No scheduling: card 4 decides *when* a poll happens, this card decides *what* one does.

Specification: `design.md` 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 4.1. Fixtures: `fixtures/README.md` sections 2, 3, 4 and 5.

### 1. `lib/parse/deals.js`

`parseDealsFeed(xml)` returns deal records in feed order, using `fast-xml-parser`. **The record shape is not yours to invent. It is pinned by `fixtures/records/deals-page0.json` and `fixtures/records/front-feed.json`, and the derivation rules are written out field by field in `fixtures/README.md` section 5.** Your parser must reproduce those files exactly.

Two things the fixtures will teach you if the README does not:

- **The node ID comes from the guid**, which reads `<id> at https://www.ozbargain.com.au`. It is identical in both feeds and it is the identity de-duplication depends on (4.1). The same deal seen in the deals feed and the front-page feed is one row, not two.
- **There is no expired flag.** The `expiry` attribute on `ozb:meta` is a timestamp, present on 92 of the 130 items in the poll corpus, and a deal is expired when that timestamp is in the past. Absent means no expiry.

A body that will not parse is a failure: record the class unparseable, retain the truncated body in `failures` (3.7), and upsert nothing from it.

### 2. `lib/time.js`

- `melbourneToUtc(day, month, year, hour, minute)` converts Australia/Melbourne wall time to UTC, **daylight-saving aware**. Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the Melbourne time zone and a long offset name to read the offset applying at a candidate instant, then correct. Do not hard-code +10:00: the corpus contains a January 2023 listing that is +11:00, and a fixed offset gets it wrong by an hour.
- `resolveRelativeAge(phrase, now)` handles `1 hour 41 min ago`, `21 hours 38 min ago`, and the day and week forms.
- `rfc822ToUtc(value)` handles the feed's pubDate format.

### 3. `lib/parse/classifieds.js`

`parseClassifiedsPage(html, options)` takes a `now` and returns the page's `uid` and its listings, using `cheerio`. Design 3.6 is the specification and `fixtures/records/classifieds.json` is the contract. Traps the corpus contains on purpose:

- **Listing 975575 has no poster.** The `/user/71488` anchor is present and its visible text is the literal string `No user info`. Treat that as an absent poster, not as a user called "No user info".
- **Both timestamp formats occur** - 16 absolute, 9 relative - and the relative form has no `on` prefix.
- **`uid` comes from the `OzB_vars` object embedded in the page.** Zero means anonymous, anything else means authenticated. This is the authoritative session check (3.6), not the status code.
- Titles are capped at 128 characters by the site. `data-title` is still the right source: the anchor's inner HTML carries `<em class="dollar">` markup and `data-title` does not.

### 4. `lib/acquire/session.js`

Classifieds session handling, three states, per 3.6:

- **Valid** - a non-zero uid and a 200 from `/classified`. Proceed.
- **Expired** - uid zero, or the application permission-denial page. **Stop polling classifieds, latch off, raise a visible alert.** Clearing the latch is a deliberate act in the UI (card 4), never automatic.
- **Cloudflare block** - stop all OzBargain requests, long backoff, loud alert.

> **Read this before writing the login flow: there is no login flow.** Open item O21 in `design.md` 12 records an unresolved conflict - 3.6 says the application logs in itself, and 3.4 puts `/user/login` on a deny list of paths *"never requested by any part of the application"*. Until the owner resolves it, **v1 takes the session cookie from settings**, supplied by the user through UI screen 9 (7.1). Do not build a login form submission, and do not remove `/user/login` from the deny list.

**Never retry a failed session in a loop.** Repeated failed logins are the pattern that gets an account flagged.

### 5. `lib/acquire/poll.js`

`runDealPoll(deps)` takes a client, store, clock and config, and performs one cycle:

- **Exactly three URLs, in this order, then stop**: deals page 0, deals page 1, front page. The list is a constant of length three. **The two-page cap is structural, not a loop bound** - there is no code path that computes a page number (3.1, D41).
- Sequential, never parallel, with the client's pause between requests.
- For each 200: parse, upsert deals, append one observation row per item - observations are written for items from *every* feed, including the front page (4.1, D46) - and set `front_page_first_seen` the first time a node is seen in the front-page feed. It cannot be recovered once missed.
- For each 304: nothing changed. Not an error. Expected to be the common case.
- Update `poll_state` with the last successful poll, the last response class and the backoff state, and record failures in `failures`.
- **Degrade rather than die** (3.7): if the front feed fails while the deals feed succeeds, the cycle commits what it got and records that front-page detection is unavailable.

`lib/acquire/classifieds.js` does the same for the single classifieds page. One page per poll, no crawling outward.

### 6. `lib/acquire/deadman.js`

Pure. `deadManState(args)` takes the last success, the current time and the last notification, and reports whether a dead-man's-switch notification is due on the decaying schedule of 3.7: 30 minutes, then 2 hours, 6 hours, then daily. Sending it is card 3's job.

## Acceptance criteria

Unless stated otherwise, tests use `createFixtureTransport` and `fixedClock`, on the poll timeline named in `fixtures/README.md` section 1.

- `parseDealsFeed` on `fixtures/http/r0.xml` deep-equals the 30 records in `fixtures/records/deals-page0.json`, and on `fixtures/http/cmp_front.xml` deep-equals the 20 in `fixtures/records/front-feed.json`. Field for field, including the UTC conversions.
- `parseClassifiedsPage` on `fixtures/http/classifieds-page.html` with the frozen now deep-equals the 25 records in `fixtures/records/classifieds.json`, and reports uid 226301.
- The type census on that page is 15 want, 8 sell, 1 free and 1 swap; 8 listings are pinned, of which 7 are want and one is the free listing 751807.
- Listing 751807 parses with pinned true and a posted time of `2023-01-17T22:33:00Z` - the AEDT case.
- Listing 975575 parses with a null poster.
- `parseClassifiedsPage` on `fixtures/http/derived/classifieds-page-anon.html` reports uid 0, and `session.js` classifies that as **expired** even though the status was 200.
- A poll cycle at POLL_1_AT against `r0.xml`, `r1.xml` and `feed_feed.xml` writes **60 deals** (30 plus 30 - the two pages do not overlap), **80 observations** (30 plus 30 plus 20, because front-page items are observed again), and sets `front_page_first_seen` on exactly 20 nodes.
- **The fixture transport is never asked for a URL containing `page=2`.** Assert it on the transport's recorded URL list, not in a comment.
- A poll cycle at POLL_2_AT where page 1 returns 304 still performs all three requests, records `not_modified` for page 1, and processes the other two.
- Node 975704 has two observation rows after polls 1 and 2, with a positive vote count of 17 and then 24.
- Node 975666 appears in the deals feed and the front-page feed at poll 1 and produces **one** row in `deals`.
- `fixtures/http/derived/deals-page0-truncated.xml` served at 200 produces zero upserts, one `failures` row classed unparseable, and does not throw out of the poll.
- `fixtures/http/derived/front-feed-promoted.xml` as the front feed at poll 1 yields node 975122 in `deals` with `front_page_first_seen` set, although it appears on neither deals page - D43.
- `deadManState` reports due at 30 minutes, not due at 29, and then follows the 2-hour, 6-hour and daily steps.

## Tests this card must include

Under `test/unit/acquisition/`: the two parser contract tests as deep-equals against the record fixtures, the time-zone helper including both the AEST and the AEDT case, relative-age resolution, session state across the three fixtures, the full poll cycle including the URL-list assertion, the mid-cycle 304, the unparseable body, the promoted front-page case, degrade-rather-than-die, and the dead-man's-switch schedule.

`test/guards/` from card 1 runs unchanged as part of this card's command.
notes:
Read `design.md` and `fixtures/README.md` before writing any code. `design.md` is normative: where it and this card disagree, `design.md` wins - say so in the PR instead of quietly choosing.

Project-wide rules, identical on every card:
- **Node.js 24 LTS. ESM JavaScript, no TypeScript.** `package.json` declares a module type and an engines floor of `>=24`.
- **SQLite is `node:sqlite`**, built into Node 24. No `better-sqlite3`, no ORM. An ExperimentalWarning on import is expected; do not change drivers because of it.
- **Tests run on `node --test`.** No Jest, Vitest, Mocha, Chai or Sinon. Node's `assert/strict` and the `node:test` mock and timer facilities are enough.
- **The test suite never reaches `ozbargain.com.au`.** Every `test:*` script must carry `--import ./test/support/no-network.js`, and a guard test asserts it does.
- **Two processes, one container** (design 2.2, D61). The Next.js server serves the UI; a separate worker owns the poll loop. **Polling from a route handler, middleware, instrumentation hook or revalidation is a build error**, not a style choice.
- Add a dependency, update `package-lock.json` in the same commit.

**The record fixtures are the contract**, derived from the real captures by `fixtures/tools/derive_records.py`. If your parser disagrees with them, re-read `fixtures/README.md` section 5 before assuming the fixture is wrong - but if you become convinced it *is* wrong, say so in the PR with the evidence rather than editing the fixture to match your parser.

The poll cycle must not import anything from `app/` or `worker/`. It receives a client, a store, a clock and config, and returns a summary. Card 4 calls it on a timer and card 5 drives it end to end.

title: Rules engine, alert ledger and suppression, notification fan-out
test_command: npm ci && npm run lint && npm run test:rules
body:
## What to build

The part of the application that decides whether something is worth telling the user about, and then tells them. Pure modules throughout: they take records, a store, a clock and a set of senders, and return decisions. Nothing here opens a socket or reads a file.

Specification: `design.md` 5 in full, 6 in full, and 3.7. Fixtures: `fixtures/README.md` sections 2 and 6 - the poll timeline and the repost threshold.

This card depends only on `foundation`. **It does not need card 2's parsers**: `fixtures/records/*.json` are real records derived from the real captures, and the tests here consume them directly.

### 1. `lib/rules/normalise.js`

Design 5.1's normalisation: lower-cased, punctuation stripped, whitespace runs collapsed, so `AMD R9700` and `amd  r9700` behave identically. Tokenisation is word-boundary anchored - **word boundaries are mandatory**, so `ple` must not match inside `simple`.

### 2. `lib/rules/match.js`

The match rule (5.1). It runs over the deal title, description text and structured category labels, and over the classifieds title, category tag and type badge.

- Default mode is **all tokens present, in any order**. Keyword mode is **any token present**.
- Items from the **front-page feed are matched as well** as items from the deals feed (D43).
- **On classifieds only `sell` listings are eligible.** `want` and `swap` never alert, and **no pinned listing ever alerts, whatever it matches** (5.1, D48). `free` is handled separately, below.
- A term pinned to a confirmed product, brand or tag slug matches that slug exactly and additively.

### 3. `lib/rules/threshold.js`

"Has reached X upvotes" (5.1). **Deals only** - classified listings carry no counters, so a threshold rule can never fire on one. Each threshold is its own rule with its own ID: a 10-vote rule and a 50-vote rule are two rules, and a deal clearing both produces two alerts. That is intended, and it is what makes muting the noisy one possible.

The window is optional. Unset means "reached X while visible". If set, **a window over 24 hours is rejected at rule entry** rather than accepted and silently never satisfied (5.1, D44).

### 4. `lib/rules/engine.js`

`evaluatePoll(args)` takes the poll's records, a store, a clock and the poll time, and returns the alerts to send plus the suppressions to record. **The order of checks is load-bearing:**

1. **Expiry first.** An expired deal never alerts, in any circumstance, **including one that became expired after it was first seen** (5.3, D45). Evaluate expiry at emit time, not only at first sight.
2. **Ledger.** Keyed on the node ID and rule ID pair; **a rule fires at most once per deal, ever** (5.2, D23). This is a permanent record, not a cooldown. A deal may legitimately alert more than once when more than one rule fires on it.
3. **Per-rule cooldown**, default 24 hours, configurable per rule, zero permitted (5.3, D25).
4. **Repost suppression.** A new deal whose normalised title is close to one already alerted under the same rule within 30 days is suppressed and recorded, not sent. **The measure is Jaccard similarity over the normalised token sets and the threshold is 0.60** - `fixtures/README.md` section 6 shows where that number comes from and the margin it sits in.
5. **Muted rules keep evaluating and keep writing ledger entries; they send nothing** (5.3). This is what makes re-enabling a rule quiet instead of a burst of stale alerts, and it is what lets the UI report how many matches happened while muted.

Gaps (5.4): a gap over 2 hours suppresses **threshold** rules for one cycle, and they resume on the next. Match rules are unaffected, because "this deal matches your term" is true regardless of how long the poller was away. Cold start on an empty database **seeds silently** - everything in the feeds is written, every rule that would have fired is marked already-alerted, **zero notifications are sent**, and a log line records the counts (D26).

Near misses and every suppression are written to the `suppressions` table for UI screen 6.

### 5. `lib/notify/`

- `provider.js` - one interface taking a title, body, URL, priority and tags. **Adding a provider must not require a change to the rules engine.**
- `email.js` (nodemailer, transport injected), `matrix.js` (one POST to the client-server API), `ntfy.js`. Each takes an injected sender; **no provider calls `globalThis.fetch` directly**, so no test in this card needs a network stub at all.
- `compose.js` - 6.3's content: the deal title, current net votes and the rate over the configured window, which rule fired and which term matched, and a link **to the `/node/<id>` page, never the `/goto/` redirect**. Exactly two controls (6.4): a rule-scoped unsubscribe labelled with the rule in the user's own words rather than a rule number, and a Manage alerts link. The unsubscribe link is an ordinary authenticated URL - **nothing in a notification is a credential.**
- `fanout.js` - **every alert is delivered through every selected provider** (6.1, D53). No priority order and no fallback chain. Failure is counted **per provider on consecutive attempts**; at five, that provider is auto-disabled, a notice is written for the UI naming the provider, the time and the last error, and **the other providers are unaffected** (6.7, D55).
- Grouping - one notification per rule per poll, listing every deal that rule matched in that poll and carrying exactly one unsubscribe control. **Grouping across rules is prohibited** (6.5): it would leave the control without an unambiguous target, and a control that silently disables the wrong rule is worse than no control.
- `freebie.js` - 6.6. The "Always notify on freebie" setting defaults **on**. Every new `free` classified listing notifies immediately without matching any rule, naming the poster and the listing. **Pinned listings are excluded even when they are freebies.** Normal priority, de-duplicated per node ID, silent on cold start, and an already-expired freebie is not announced.
- **Front-page alerts carry the highest priority** (6.3). Every other alert is normal.
- `deadman.js` - sends what card 2's `deadManState` reports as due.

## Acceptance criteria

Every number below is real, drawn from the corpus, and asserted with a frozen clock.

- **Cross-feed de-duplication.** A match rule on `torbox` evaluated over poll 1's three feeds produces **one** alert and **one** ledger row, although node 975666 appears in both the deals feed and the front-page feed.
- **Expiry beats matching.** A match rule on `ubiquiti` at poll 1 matches 975704, which is live, and 975700, which expired at `2026-09-19T05:29:06Z`. Exactly **one** alert is sent and one `suppressions` row of kind expired is written.
- **Expiry beats thresholds.** A threshold rule at 27 upvotes over polls 1 and 2 does **not** fire on node 975702, which rises from 26 to 28 but expired at `2026-09-19T05:51:28Z`. A match rule on `noctua` never fires on it either, at any poll.
- **Thresholds fire once.** A threshold rule at 20 upvotes does not fire at poll 1, when 975704 has 17 votes; fires exactly once at poll 2, when it has 24; and does not fire again at poll 3. The ledger holds exactly one row for that node and rule pair - acceptance criterion 11.3.1.
- **Two thresholds, two alerts.** Rules at 20 and at 100 upvotes over the same polls produce two independent ledger rows for a deal clearing both.
- **Cooldown.** A keyword rule on `ubiquiti, fuel` with a 24-hour cooldown fires at poll 1 on 975704 and is **suppressed at poll 2** on the newly appeared 975721, with a `suppressions` row of kind cooldown. With the cooldown set to zero it fires both times.
- **Repost suppression.** Over the 25 classifieds records, listings 975593 and 975574 score 0.667 and the second is suppressed under the same rule. **No other pair in the corpus reaches 0.60** - assert that across every pair, so the threshold is regression-tested from both sides.
- **Muted rules.** A muted rule that matches writes its ledger row and sends nothing, and re-enabling it does not fire retroactively for matches that happened while muted (11.3.4).
- **Classifieds eligibility.** Over `fixtures/records/classifieds.json`, a match rule broad enough to hit every listing alerts on **at most the 8 sell listings** and never on a want, a swap, or a pinned listing.
- **Freebies.** The raw classifieds page produces **zero** freebie notifications, because its only freebie - 751807 - is pinned and dated January 2023. `fixtures/http/derived/classifieds-page-unpinned-freebie.html` produces **exactly one**, naming the poster `ausdkunst`, at normal priority, carrying the same two controls as any other alert.
- **Cold start.** Seeding an empty database from poll 1 sends **zero** notifications while writing the deals, the observations and the already-alerted ledger rows (11.4.5).
- **Fan-out.** With three providers selected, one alert produces three send attempts. A provider that fails five consecutive times is disabled and a UI notice records the provider, the time and the last error, while **the other two keep delivering**. A success before the fifth failure resets the counter.
- **Grouping.** A rule matching three deals in one poll produces **one** notification listing three deals and carrying **one** unsubscribe control. Two rules matching in the same poll produce two notifications, never one merged notification.
- **Gaps.** With a three-hour gap before the poll, threshold rules are suppressed for one cycle and resume on the next, while match rules fire normally throughout.
- **Links.** No composed notification contains a `/goto/` URL. Assert it over every notification every test in this card produces.

## Tests this card must include

Under `test/unit/rules/`: normalisation and word boundaries, both matching modes, classifieds eligibility, threshold firing and the 24-hour window rejection, the ledger, cooldown, repost similarity across every corpus pair, expiry in both orders, muting, gaps, cold-start seeding, grouping, fan-out and per-provider failure counting, the freebie class in both directions, priority, and the `/goto/` prohibition.

`test/guards/` from card 1 runs unchanged as part of this card's command.
notes:
Read `design.md` and `fixtures/README.md` before writing any code. `design.md` is normative: where it and this card disagree, `design.md` wins - say so in the PR instead of quietly choosing.

Project-wide rules, identical on every card:
- **Node.js 24 LTS. ESM JavaScript, no TypeScript.** `package.json` declares a module type and an engines floor of `>=24`.
- **SQLite is `node:sqlite`**, built into Node 24. No `better-sqlite3`, no ORM. An ExperimentalWarning on import is expected; do not change drivers because of it.
- **Tests run on `node --test`.** No Jest, Vitest, Mocha, Chai or Sinon. Node's `assert/strict` and the `node:test` mock and timer facilities are enough.
- **The test suite never reaches `ozbargain.com.au`.** Every `test:*` script must carry `--import ./test/support/no-network.js`, and a guard test asserts it does.
- **Two processes, one container** (design 2.2, D61). The Next.js server serves the UI; a separate worker owns the poll loop. **Polling from a route handler, middleware, instrumentation hook or revalidation is a build error**, not a style choice.
- Add a dependency, update `package-lock.json` in the same commit.

**Do not wait for card 2.** `fixtures/records/deals-page0.json`, `front-feed.json` and `classifieds.json` are real parsed records, and the poll timeline is documented in `fixtures/README.md` section 1. Build the engine against those. The vote movements between polls (975704 goes 17 to 24, 975702 goes 26 to 28) are real changes between two real captures 35 minutes apart, which is why the threshold tests here need no invented data.

Every provider takes an injected sender. If a test in this card ever makes the network guard fire, something is wired wrong.

title: The two processes: the worker that owns the poll loop, and the Next.js UI
test_command: npm ci && npm run lint && npm run test:web
body:
## What to build

The two long-lived processes of design 2.2, and the guard tests that keep them apart.

Specification: `design.md` 2.2, 7 in full, 8.2, 8.3, 8.6, 9.2, 3.7. Decisions: D61, D62, D63.

### Read this first

**Next.js has no scheduler.** This application's heart is a poll loop running every five minutes. Nothing in the framework will run it, and the request lifecycle is the wrong place to look for one.

So: **the poll loop lives in a separate worker process.** Not in a route handler. Not in `instrumentation.js`. Not behind an on-demand revalidation, a cron route, or a `setInterval` at module scope in the server bundle. A poll driven by an HTTP request happens only when somebody is looking at the application - which is exactly when the user does not need it, and never at 3 a.m. when the deal is posted.

This card ships a test that fails if that ever changes. Do not weaken it.

### 1. `lib/scheduler.js`

`createScheduler(deps)` takes a clock and injectable timer functions, giving a small timer wheel that is testable without waiting. It must:

- run a task on a fixed interval, correcting for drift so a slow tick does not shift every later one;
- **never overlap a task with itself** - if a poll is still running when the next is due, skip that beat and record it;
- survive a task that throws, log it, and keep the schedule;
- stop cleanly on request.

### 2. `worker/main.js`

The worker process, and the composition root. It opens the store, builds the real transport, the client, the rules engine and the providers from config, and registers:

- the **deal poll** every `OZB_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, default 300;
- the **classifieds poll** every `OZB_CLASSIFIEDS_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, default 3600;
- the **dead-man's-switch check**, and the notification when one is due (3.7);
- a **nightly** job running `pruneObservations` and `writeSnapshot` (4.2, 4.3).

It handles `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` by stopping the scheduler, letting an in-flight tick finish, closing the database and exiting 0. It binds no port. On an unrecoverable error it exits non-zero, and card 5's entrypoint takes the container down with it - because a container with a dead poller and a live UI looks exactly like a quiet day.

### 3. `middleware.js` - Cloudflare Access verification

Design 8.2: **the application verifies the Access JWT on every request, without exception.** Middleware is the right home - one file, applied to every route by default, rather than a check each new route handler has to remember (D63). The constraints that follow are binding:

- **Use `jose`.** Middleware does not run with the full Node.js API surface available, so a library built on Node's `crypto` module is not a candidate. Verify RS256 against Cloudflare's remote JWKS with `createRemoteJWKSet`, which caches keys; do not fetch the JWKS on every request.
- Check the **audience** against `CF_ACCESS_AUD` and the **issuer** against `CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN`. Take identity from the verified `email` claim. Read the token from the `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` header **or** the `CF_Authorization` cookie.
- **Never infer that a request came through Access from the network path** (8.2). The LAN path exists by design, and this verification is what makes it harmless. It is load-bearing, not defence in depth.
- **The matcher must not exclude `/_next/static`.** The conventional Next.js matcher does. Acceptance criterion 11.2.4 requires that a static asset requested with no session is not a 200, so that exclusion cannot be used here.
- There are exactly two exemptions (8.3, D62): the **icon route**, exempt only when `OZB_ICON_ROUTE_PUBLIC` is set (Open Item O15), and **`/healthz`**, which authenticates with the container-local `OZB_HEALTHCHECK_SECRET` in a header. `/healthz` is therefore not an unauthenticated path, and a LAN request to it without the secret is rejected like anything else.

### 4. `lib/csrf.js` and the mutation routes

**CSRF protection on every state-changing request** (7.2, 8.6, D33). Access authenticates the visitor, not the origin of the request, and the `SameSite` behaviour of the Access cookie is not relied upon. Implement a signed double-submit token using Web Crypto - no dependency needed. Every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE verifies it.

### 5. `app/` - the nine screens

All nine ship (7.1, D52). Nothing is cut:

1. **Status** - acquisition health first: last successful poll, last response class, current backoff state. A visible last-checked timestamp appears on **every page of the application**.
2. **Rules list** - enabled, muted or snoozed state; match counts over 7 and 30 days; last fired; cooldown; optional pinned slug; and which surfaces the rule applies to, fixed to deals-only for threshold rules and not editable.
3. **Rule create, edit and delete** - full CRUD over term text, matching mode, cooldown and surfaces.
4. **Rule state control** - enable, mute, snooze, re-enable. The route `/rules/<id>/mute` is the unsubscribe target from 6.4, gated exactly like every other path, and **muting suppresses that rule's already-queued rows in `pending_alerts`**. The confirmation offers undo in one tap, and snooze for 24 hours, 7 days, or keep it off. **Mute, never delete.**
5. **Alert history** - what fired, when, under which rule, for which deal or listing, with a link.
6. **Near-miss and suppression log** - reads the `suppressions` table.
7. **Threshold configuration** - editable.
8. **Delivery configuration** - provider selection, credentials, and a **test-send button**. A test send happens in the Next.js process: that is a request, not a schedule, and it is the one place the server may send a notification.
9. **Classifieds session status** - validity, when it was last confirmed working, and somewhere to supply a fresh session cookie. This is where card 2's expired-session latch is cleared, by hand.

Plus `/healthz`, which reports **unhealthy when the last successful poll is older than three poll intervals** (3.7). Acquisition health, not process liveness.

**The UI is operable on a phone** (7.2). Every notification links to it and notifications are read on a phone. Settings edited here land in `settings` and `rules`, not in environment variables (D51).

## Acceptance criteria

- **The architecture guard passes.** A test walks every file under `app/` and `middleware.js` and asserts that none of them imports `lib/acquire/`, `lib/scheduler.js` or anything under `worker/`, and that none contains `setInterval`. A second assertion checks that `worker/main.js` does import `lib/acquire/poll.js`. If a later change moves polling into a route, this test fails - that is its entire purpose.
- The scheduler, driven by `node:test` fake timers, runs a task once per interval; a task taking longer than one interval causes exactly one skipped beat, recorded, rather than a queue of overlapping runs; a throwing task does not stop the schedule; and drift does not accumulate over 20 ticks.
- `worker/main.js` started against a temporary database and a fixture transport performs a poll, and on `SIGTERM` exits 0 with the database closed cleanly.
- Middleware, called directly with a Request:
  - no token gives not-200;
  - a token signed by a **locally generated** key served from a loopback JWKS, with the right audience and issuer, passes, and the verified `email` claim is available downstream;
  - right signature but **wrong audience** is rejected;
  - right signature but **wrong issuer** is rejected;
  - an expired token is rejected;
  - a request to `/_next/static/anything` with no token gives not-200 (11.2.4);
  - `/healthz` with the correct secret header is allowed, and **without it is rejected**;
  - the icon route is exempt only when `OZB_ICON_ROUTE_PUBLIC` is set.
- An unauthenticated POST to a rule-editing route is rejected and the rule is unchanged (11.3.6). A POST carrying a valid JWT but **no CSRF token** is also rejected: the two checks are independent.
- Muting a rule marks it disabled rather than deleting it, and removes that rule's rows from `pending_alerts`.
- `/healthz` reports healthy when `poll_state` shows a poll within three intervals, and unhealthy at three intervals plus one second.
- A rules-list request renders without error against a store seeded from `fixtures/records/`, and the last-checked timestamp is present on every rendered page.

## Tests this card must include

Under `test/unit/web/`: the scheduler with fake timers across all four behaviours, the worker's startup and shutdown, every middleware case above, CSRF, the mute route including `pending_alerts` suppression, `/healthz` in both states, and one render test per screen sufficient to prove it does not throw against seeded data.

Under `test/guards/`: `architecture.test.js`, the no-polling-in-the-server-tree check described above. It joins the permanent guard set and runs with every card's command from here on.

`test/guards/` from card 1 runs unchanged.
notes:
Read `design.md` and `fixtures/README.md` before writing any code. `design.md` is normative: where it and this card disagree, `design.md` wins - say so in the PR instead of quietly choosing.

Project-wide rules, identical on every card:
- **Node.js 24 LTS. ESM JavaScript, no TypeScript.** `package.json` declares a module type and an engines floor of `>=24`.
- **SQLite is `node:sqlite`**, built into Node 24. No `better-sqlite3`, no ORM. An ExperimentalWarning on import is expected; do not change drivers because of it.
- **Tests run on `node --test`.** No Jest, Vitest, Mocha, Chai or Sinon. Node's `assert/strict` and the `node:test` mock and timer facilities are enough.
- **The test suite never reaches `ozbargain.com.au`.** Every `test:*` script must carry `--import ./test/support/no-network.js`, and a guard test asserts it does.
- **Two processes, one container** (design 2.2, D61). The Next.js server serves the UI; a separate worker owns the poll loop. **Polling from a route handler, middleware, instrumentation hook or revalidation is a build error**, not a style choice.
- Add a dependency, update `package-lock.json` in the same commit.

**The single most important property of this card is that the poll loop is not in the Next.js process.** If you find yourself reaching for `instrumentation.js`, a cron route, or a `setInterval` in a layout, stop: that is the failure this card exists to prevent, and the architecture guard will fail the build.

The JWKS in tests is generated locally with Web Crypto and served on `127.0.0.1`. Loopback is the only host the network guard permits, and Cloudflare's real JWKS endpoint is never contacted.

Both processes open the same SQLite file. Card 1 set the busy timeout; rely on it rather than inventing a lock.

title: Integration: assemble both processes, package the image, ship the pipeline, run the whole suite
test_command: npm ci && npm run lint && npm test
body:
## What to build

The card that turns the other four into an application: the container that runs both processes, the pipeline that publishes it, the template that deploys it, and an end-to-end suite that exercises the whole chain against real captured responses.

Specification: `design.md` 2.2, 10 in full, 11 in full.

### 1. `Dockerfile` and `docker-entrypoint.sh`

Multi-stage, on `node:24-alpine`, using the standalone build output card 1 configured. The image:

- runs as a **non-root user**;
- exposes port **8000**;
- carries OCI labels including `org.opencontainers.image.source` (10.4);
- writes nothing of value inside the container - **all persistent state lives on the bind mount at `/data`** (10.6);
- declares a healthcheck calling `127.0.0.1:8000/healthz` with the container-local secret (D62).

`docker-entrypoint.sh` is the supervisor, and it is the whole reason this application is not a single process:

- it starts **both** the Next.js server and `worker/main.js`;
- it forwards `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` to both children;
- it **exits non-zero the moment either child exits**, so Docker restarts the container.

A container with a live UI and a dead poller is the failure mode that looks exactly like a quiet day (6.7). The supervisor exists so that it cannot happen quietly.

### 2. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

Design 10.4, exactly:

1. lint - ESLint;
2. unit tests - `node --test`;
3. build the image, **on every trigger including pull requests**;
4. **smoke test the built image**;
5. publish, **only on `main`, and only if 1 to 4 passed**.

Pull requests run 1 to 4 and publish nothing. A **concurrency group keyed on the branch reference with cancel-in-progress** is mandatory, so two rapid pushes cannot finish out of order and leave `:latest` pointing at the older commit. `linux/amd64` only. GitHub Actions build cache. Node 24, installing with `npm ci`.

It publishes exactly two tags to `ghcr.io/jamesgallagher/ozbargainhunter`: `:latest` and `:main-<sha>`. No beta, stable or semantic-version tags (10.2, D2). **Branch protection is unavailable on this account, so the deployment is the gate rather than the merge** - publishing must be conditional on the tests passing, so a failing commit cannot reach the host. This is mandatory, not optional (10.4).

### 3. `unraid/my-OzBargainHunter.xml`

The canonical copy of the template (10.6): container name `OzBargainHunter`, repository `ghcr.io/jamesgallagher/ozbargainhunter:latest` - a **moving** tag, because a pinned one never produces an update - `/mnt/user/appdata/ozbargain-hunter/` mapped to `/data`, port 8000 published, and the environment variables of 9.1. The icon field points at a hosted copy of `icon-256.png`; the assets are in `assets/logo/` and the hosting is Open Item O15, so leave a documented placeholder rather than inventing a URL.

### 4. `scripts/fixture-server.mjs`

A loopback HTTP server that serves the corpus as though it were OzBargain: it maps the three poll URLs to fixture files, advances through the poll timeline on successive requests, honours `If-None-Match` by returning a real 304, and serves the classifieds page. It is what both the integration suite and the CI smoke test point the application at, and **it listens on `127.0.0.1` only.**

### 5. `test/integration/`

The real integration work, all of it against fixtures and a temporary database:

- **The three-poll scenario.** Cold start on an empty database at POLL_1_AT seeds silently and sends zero notifications. Poll 2 at POLL_2_AT fires the alerts that should fire. Poll 3 at POLL_3_AT gets three 304 responses and sends nothing. Rules configured: a match rule on `ubiquiti`, a match rule on `torbox`, a threshold rule at 20 upvotes, and the freebie setting on.
- **Both processes, for real.** Spawn the Next.js server and `worker/main.js` as two child processes against one temporary database and the fixture server, with a short poll interval. **Make no HTTP request to the application at all.** After two intervals, assert the database has gained observations. This is the proof that polling is not request-driven, and it is the single most important assertion in the suite.
- **The live server and its middleware.** With both processes up: an unauthenticated request is not a 200; a request carrying a JWT signed by a locally generated key served from a loopback JWKS is a 200 and the log shows the verified `email` claim; a static asset requested with no session is not a 200; and `/healthz` reports healthy once the fixture-fed poll has succeeded.
- **Packaging assertions that need no Docker.** Parse the `Dockerfile`, `docker-entrypoint.sh`, `ci.yml` and `unraid/my-OzBargainHunter.xml` and assert their required properties: base image, non-root user, exposed port, healthcheck, both children started, signals trapped, the five jobs in order, the concurrency group with cancel-in-progress, exactly two tags, the publish condition, the bind mount, and the moving tag. These run on any machine.

### 6. `scripts/smoke-image.mjs`

What CI job 4 runs, and what a developer with Docker can run locally: start the fixture server, run the built image against it with the feed URLs pointed at loopback, wait for the health check to go healthy, then assert that an unauthenticated request is not a 200, that a properly signed one is a 200, and that **the database has gained observations although no request was made to the application until that moment.**

**The smoke test does not touch `ozbargain.com.au`, and could not pass if it did**: the health check reports unhealthy until a poll has succeeded, so a smoke test with no reachable feed could only pass by making the health check meaningless.

### 7. `npm test`

Runs the unit tests of cards 1 to 4, the guards, and this card's integration tests, in one command, with the network guard imported. This is the card's gate, and it is CI job 2.

## Acceptance criteria

- `npm ci && npm run lint && npm test` passes from a clean checkout on Node 24, **with no network access to anything but loopback**.
- The three-poll scenario, asserted end to end against the resulting database and the captured notifications:
  - poll 1 sends **zero** notifications and writes 60 deals and 80 observations;
  - the `ubiquiti` rule sends **one** notification, for 975704 - 975700 matches but is expired, and a `suppressions` row of kind expired records it;
  - the `torbox` rule sends **one** notification, although 975666 is in both feeds;
  - the 20-vote threshold rule sends **nothing** at poll 1 and **one** notification at poll 2, when 975704 reaches 24;
  - 975704 gains `front_page_first_seen` at poll 2 and its front-page alert carries the **highest** priority;
  - poll 3 is three 304 responses and sends nothing;
  - the ledger holds exactly one row per node-and-rule pair across all three polls;
  - no notification anywhere contains a `/goto/` URL.
- **The unwatched-poll assertion**: with both processes running and zero HTTP requests made to the application, `observations` is non-empty after two poll intervals.
- The live-server access-control assertions all hold, matching acceptance criteria 11.2.1 to 11.2.4.
- The fixture server records that the application requested **exactly three URLs per poll cycle**, in the order deals page 0, deals page 1, front page, and **never** one containing `page=2`.
- The packaging assertions pass on a machine without Docker.
- `npm run smoke:image` passes where Docker is available. Its absence does not fail `npm test`; CI always runs it.

## Tests this card must include

Under `test/integration/`: the three-poll scenario, the two-process unwatched-poll test, the live-server middleware and CSRF tests, the fixture server's conditional-request behaviour, and the four packaging-artifact assertions.

All of `test/unit/` and all of `test/guards/` run as part of `npm test`. **This card is not done until every test from every card passes in one command.**
notes:
Read `design.md` and `fixtures/README.md` before writing any code. `design.md` is normative: where it and this card disagree, `design.md` wins - say so in the PR instead of quietly choosing.

Project-wide rules, identical on every card:
- **Node.js 24 LTS. ESM JavaScript, no TypeScript.** `package.json` declares a module type and an engines floor of `>=24`.
- **SQLite is `node:sqlite`**, built into Node 24. No `better-sqlite3`, no ORM. An ExperimentalWarning on import is expected; do not change drivers because of it.
- **Tests run on `node --test`.** No Jest, Vitest, Mocha, Chai or Sinon. Node's `assert/strict` and the `node:test` mock and timer facilities are enough.
- **The test suite never reaches `ozbargain.com.au`.** Every `test:*` script must carry `--import ./test/support/no-network.js`, and a guard test asserts it does.
- **Two processes, one container** (design 2.2, D61). The Next.js server serves the UI; a separate worker owns the poll loop. **Polling from a route handler, middleware, instrumentation hook or revalidation is a build error**, not a style choice.
- Add a dependency, update `package-lock.json` in the same commit.

This is the integration card. Its job is to find the seams the other four got wrong, so expect to fix small things in `lib/` rather than papering over them here - but do not redesign anything. If an earlier card's module is wrong, fix it and say so in the PR.

The two-process test spawns real child processes with a short poll interval, and card 1 rejects anything below 300 seconds. **Add the test-only override in this card**: a separate variable, `OZB_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS_TEST_OVERRIDE`, that `lib/config.js` honours **only** when the environment is `test`, covered by a test asserting it is ignored otherwise. Do not lower the floor itself - design 3.2 is explicit that the real interval is never below five minutes.

Docker may not be available in the build environment. Every assertion that matters is reachable without it; `smoke:image` is the only thing that needs it, and CI is where it always runs.
